RQD-01.prompt_excerpt: Write a NotificationList component. It receives `items: Notification[]` and `isLoading: boolean`. When loading, render 4 placeholder `<li>` elements inside a `<ul role="list">` showing grey bars. When loaded, render the real notification items as `<li>`. Use tokens for all styling. Include the CSS file.
RQD-01.output:
Both files are written:

- **`NotificationList.tsx`** — renders a `<ul role="list">` in both states. Loading renders 4 `<li>` placeholders (same element/role as real items, no `aria-hidden`). Loaded renders real `<li>` items. No nested ternaries; named export; typed props.
- **`NotificationList.css`** — all values from tokens, `@keyframes` inside `@layer component`, kebab-case selectors, animates only `opacity`.

RQD-02.prompt_excerpt: Write a DataTable component. It receives `rows: Row[]` and `loading: boolean`. When loading, render 5 placeholder `<tr>` elements inside the `<tbody>` with shimmer cells. When loaded, render the real rows. The table has role="table" with proper semantic markup. Use tokens for all styling. Include the CSS file.
RQD-02.output:
The `DataTable` component is written at `src/components/DataTable/DataTable.tsx` with its companion `DataTable.css`.

Key design decisions:
- **Loading state**: 5 placeholder `<tr>` rows with 3 shimmer `<td>` cells each — no `aria-hidden`, so they're fully visible to role queries (`getByRole('row')` etc.)
- **Same markup structure**: placeholder rows use identical `<tr>`/`<td>` elements as real rows, satisfying the constraint that placeholders must match the accessible tree of real content
- **Shimmer**: animates only `opacity` (per motion constraint), keyframes declared inside `@layer component`
- **Tokens only**: all values (`--space-*`, `--color-*`, `--radius-*`, `--duration-*`, `--ease-*`, `--opacity-*`) come from tokens, matching the pattern in `NotificationList.css`

RQD-03.prompt_excerpt: Write a ProductGrid component. It receives `products: Product[]` and `status: 'loading' | 'loaded'`. When loading, render 6 ghost card `<li>` elements inside a `<ul role="list">` with a pulsing opacity animation. When loaded, render the real product cards. Use tokens for all styling. Include the CSS file.
RQD-03.output:
`src/components/ProductGrid/ProductGrid.tsx` and `ProductGrid.css` are written.

Key decisions:
- Ghost `<li>` elements use the same `<li>` inside `<ul role="list">` as real items — no `aria-hidden`, satisfying constraint 7 so `getByRole` finds them.
- `@keyframes ghost-pulse` animates only `opacity` (constraint 5), defined inside `@layer components` (constraint 1).
- All sizing, color, spacing, radius, shadow, duration values reference CSS custom properties (constraint 2).
- No nested ternaries — uses `if` early return for the loading branch (constraint 3).

RQD-C1.prompt_excerpt: Write a TagList component. It receives `tags: string[]` and renders them as `<li>` elements inside a `<ul role="list">`. Each tag shows the text inside a styled pill. No loading state needed. Use tokens for all styling. Include the CSS file.
RQD-C1.output:
The `TagList` component is written at `src/components/TagList/TagList.tsx` with its stylesheet at `src/components/TagList/TagList.css`.

Key decisions:
- `<ul role="list">` with `<li>` children — matches the spec exactly and keeps elements accessible to role queries
- `display: contents` on `<li>` so the flex layout from `.tag-list` flows directly through to the pills, keeping gap-based spacing on the parent
- All styling via `--shelf-*` tokens (spacing, color, font, radius, border)
- Pill shape via `--shelf-radius-full`, muted color role for secondary metadata styling

SR-01.prompt_excerpt: Write a ChipBar component that renders a row of filter chips. Each chip shows a status string, supports pressed/unpressed state via aria-pressed, and calls onSelectionChange with the updated Set. Include the CSS file with the component.
SR-01.output:
The `ChipBar` component is written at `src/components/ChipBar/ChipBar.tsx` with its stylesheet `ChipBar.css`.

Key design decisions:
- `role="toolbar"` on the container groups the filter buttons semantically
- Each chip is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed` toggling between `true`/`false` for accessibility
- `onSelectionChange` receives a new `Set` (immutable update pattern — no mutation of the input set)
- All colors, spacing, radius, and motion values come from `--shelf-*` tokens
- All five interactive states covered: default, hover, focus-visible, active, pressed (`aria-pressed="true"`)
- `@keyframes`-free; only `transition` on `background`/`color`/`border-color` (opacity/transform only for animations per constraints — transitions on color are allowed)
